Generate plotting data for Bayesian item response theory models

Source: R/BayesIRTdata.R
BayesIRTdata.Rd

Generate plotting data for Bayesian item response theory (IRT) models fitted in blavaan. BayesIRTdata() reads in a fitted IRT model from blavaan. The current version supports unidimensional two-parameter IRT models for binary items. The generated datasets may be used for the following types of plots: Item-Person Map (IPM), Item Characteristic Curve (ICC), Item Information Curve (IIC), Test Characteristic Curve (TCC), Test Information Curve (TIC), and Marginal Reliability Plot (REL).

Usage

BayesIRTdata(blavaanobj)

Arguments

blavaanobj

A fitted IRT model from blavaan.

Value

A list of model information, summary data, and summary statistics used for plotting. The latent trait (theta) values are evaluated over a range of -6 to 6.

nitems

Number of items in the fitted model.

draws_by_item_theta

Posterior draws of item discrimination (a) and item threshold (tau) parameters, along with calculated probabilities of a correct response (p) and item information (i) across theta values.

The IRT models fitted in blavaan are on probit scale. Item discrimination (a) parameters are converted to logit scale and are used to calculate the probabilities of a correct response and item information. Item threshold (tau) parameters remain on the probit scale.

summary_by_item

Summary of item threshold (tau) parameters across posterior draws. Statistics include mean, Q1, median (Q2), Q3, and the lower and upper whiskers (calculated as Q1 − 1.5 × IQR and Q3 + 1.5 × IQR, respectively).

summary_by_item_theta

Mean probabilities of a correct response (p) and mean item information (i) across posterior draws, by item and theta.

summary_by_draw_theta

Expected test scores (test_p) and test information (test_i), by posterior draw and theta.

summary_by_theta

Mean expected test scores (test_p) and mean test information (test_i) across posterior draws, by theta.

summary_by_draw

Marginal reliability for each posterior draw. Reliability is calculated at each theta value, then averaged across theta values using standard normal distribution density weights.

mean_reliability

Marginal reliability calculated from the mean test information across posterior draws. Reliability at each theta value is calculated using the mean test information across posterior draws, then averaged across theta values using standard normal distribution density weights.

Examples

# access individual dataset
data <- BayesIRTdata(tma.IRT.fitted.model)
data$summary_by_item
